properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/10/2021 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Winslow Twp, Jefferson county. SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/10/2021
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 929444
Permit API: 065-25527
Unconventional: No
County: Jefferson
Municipality: Winslow Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/10/2021
Comments: This well was drilled in a forested area off of Point View Road in March 2006. Since the most recent inspection of the site on 8/30/2021 (Inspection Record # 3242810), work has been started on remediation of the site. A spill was reported to the Department on 11:03 AM on August 27, 2021. The spill occurred from a broken copper line attached to the wellhead. The estimated volume lost from this spill was 2 bbl. During this inspection, it was noted that the production equipment has been disconnected and staged along the edge of the restored site. Stressed vegetation and contaminated soil has been removed from the site. A response to the NOV has been received by the Department. The response states that five tri-axle loads of contaminated soil and vegetation were removed from the site. The response also states that the excavation will be left open until the attainment of standards from the Alternative Remediation Process has been demonstrated. The violations at the site can be closed when the contaminated soil has been replaced, the site has been graded to final contours, and the manifest and tipping information for soil disposal has been received by the Department.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 1/24/2023 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/24/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 983063
Permit API: 081-21881
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/24/2023
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions on both well pads and the access road. Both pads and the access road were snow-covered during this inspection. Along the access road, the orange construction fence is damaged in many locations. The metal poles have been bent by truck traffic in multiple locations. A work crew was working on the temporary E and S BMPs along the access road during this inspection. I met with NFG representative Colby Dynda during this inspection. He said that he was directing the crew to replace the damaged temporary E and S BMPs and to install new temporary E and S BMPs during this inspection. He said that additional compost filter sock and silt fence had been installed at stream crossings and wetlands. On Pad B, most of the equipment for the frac has been removed from the pad. The MASS remains on the pad. The area northwest of the MASS where fluid with elevated conductivity was snow-covered but appeared to be dry. The area northeast of the MASS had some slush present which had an electrical conductivity ranging between 5.31 and 9.11 mS/cm. A portable pump and a fuel can is present near the sump at the northeast outlet of the north stormwater channel. The Department recommends putting the pump and the fuel can on secondary containment. On Pad A, six wells are staged for production. Six GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs and containment appear to be in good condition. Violations remain outstanding for 12/19/22 produced fluid release to Pad B.

properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 9/17/2025 to EQT PROD CO in Morris Township, Greene county. 78a55(b) - CONTROL AND DISPOSAL PLANNING  – PPC Plan - Operator failed to prepare and develop a site specific PPC plan prior to storing, using, or generating regulated substances on a well site from the drilling, alteration, production, plugging or other activity associated with a gas well or transporting those regulated substances to, on or from a well site.

Violation ID: 8249209
Permit API: 059-27655
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/17/2025
Comments: On 09/17/2025, an incident inspection was conducted at the Harden Farms Well Site following receipt of an incident report that was submitted to the Department on 09/17/2025 at 12:17 (CTS 392314).It was reported that 10 gallons of biocide material was spilled on site at 12:00, 09/17/2025. No waterways were affected. It was also reported that a clean up crew (SPSI) was on site.I called the EQT representative who reported the spill, Lance Witters, for information. I noted that SPSI arrived after I did, and I requested the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) to be sent to me. It was described to me that the material spilled was a Multi-Chem biocide. The cause of the release was that a hose back pressured, biocide flowed back to the tank, and the tank overflowed. It was estimated that 10 gallons spilled.SPSI had not began remediation and was not on the pad when I arrived. No personal were on the pad upon my arrival.The following was observed:The contaminated area was adjacent to the gas production units (GPUs). It was unknown if any production fluid was present in addition to the biocide spilled; no elevated conductivity was observed. No remediation had begun and SPSI was not on the pad when I arrived on the pad. SPSI arrived to the site after the Department (Photo 1). An extremely strong odor was experienced on site in the vicinity of the contaminated area.SPSI then arrived on the pad and had not begun remediation while I was on site. The impacted area was located between the well heads and the GPUs. The impacted area appeared wet with small sections of pooled fluid (Photos 2-5).I asked SPSI if they had the SDS, and they did not. The SDS was not located on site with the site documents in the mailboxes. I was able to locate a Control and Disposal Plan and the Site Specific Safety and Environmental Plan and Policy. I was not able to locate any information related to the Multi-Chem biocide (Photos 6-9). I also did not find a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan (PPC) on site. The SDSs are required to be on site. The PPC Plan is also required to be on site during drilling or completion activities, however the well operator shall prepare and develop a site specific PPC plan prior to storing, using, or generating regulated substances to, on or from a well site.The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance (Photo 10).The Department requests a description of the activities that were being carried out that resulted in a spill.Due to the SDS not present on site, a PPC Plan not on site, failure to control regulated fluids with a release to the ground, and failure to use secondary containment, violations of 78a.54, 78a55(a), 78a55(b), 78a55(i)5iD, SWMA 301, 91.34(a), and 78a64a(b) are being issued.

Violation ID: 8245069

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/12/2025
Comments: On August 12, 2025, the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of Range Resources Conner Samuel well site, located in Cecil Township, Washington County in response to a spill that was reported to the DEP hotline on 8/11/2025 at 8:44pm by Range. Accompanying on today's inspection is Range Resources representative Kevin Rudd.According to the report and Mr. Rudd, after finishing the cement job on the 4H, a flow line became over pressurized due to a valve being left closed. This resulted in a 10 cap dislodging from the flow line and releasing approximately 21 gallons of a synthetic oil based mud (SOBM) fine mist on to the graveled well pad and approximately 42 gallons on to the secondary containment. According to Range, prior to this inspection, the fine mist release was remediated in accordance with 78a66(c)(1) and disposal documents will be provided to the Department upon its receipt.At the time of this inspection, the Act 9 Sign was observed at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it, and in the on-site mailbox was the Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency Plan, both of which had all required components. The access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel and the well site perimeters were observed to be exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the release area to be approximately 12ft x 20ft and comprised of had freshly laid gravel. No SOBM was observed on the gravel or on the secondary containment in this area at the time of this inspection. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the gravel well pad in this release area, and collected soil conductivity readings of 0.0002 mS, in three different locations as well as 0.0651 mS, and 0.0028 mS. These soil conductivity readings are comparable to the background soil conductivity reading of 0.0213 mS, which was collected upslope and adjacent to the well site in a vegetated area.At the time of this inspection, the Department requested Safety Data Sheets (SDSs) for the SOBM involved in the release as well as secondary containment inspection logs. At the time of this inspection, Mr. Rudd provided the Department with the secondary containment logs and attempted to email the Department an electronic copy of the SDSs, however, that email was not received, therefore the Department is again requesting that SDSs for the SOBM be provided to the Department within 2 business days of the receipt of this inspection report.Based on observations made at the time of this inspection, it appears that Range remediated the release in accordance with 78a66(c)(1), therefore, violations are noted and immediately corrected.Transmittal of this inspection report is delayed due to an app IT error.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARD OPR LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/10/2021
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 907829
Permit API: 081-21846
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/10/2021
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that drilling mud sprayed from a flare stack during a gas kick which impacted the pad surface and an adjacent area within the LOD on February 6, 2021. The site was snow-covered during this inspection. DEP EP Specialist Justin Abbott accompanied me on this inspection. We met with company man Bill Mitchell upon arriving on location. The rig is finishing the 2nd of 5 wells on the pad. The release occurred while the cementing the A-1H well. According to the company man on location, the drilling mud sprayed northeast of the flare stack. The mud spray landed on containment, in the travel lane along the northeast edge of the pad, and in the area within the LOD along the northeast side of the pad. Impacted snow was removed by skid steer and with shovels. The impacted snow was placed in a container for disposal. The mud residue could be observed on the well site secondary containment, on a battery of frac tanks, on several chemical totes, and on a light cover. No residue was observed on the pad surface or anywhere off of the pad. New snowfall the day before this inspection made an examination of the pad surface and the soil off of the pad difficult. According to an email sent on February 11, 2021 to the Department, Rick Hall of ARD stated that most of what impacted the snow off of the secondary containment was ash from drilling mud that was combusted by the flare stack. He stated that based on a minimal amount of fluid off containment, the small area impacted, and interviews with the company man and cleanup personnel, that the estimated release volume is less than 5 gallons. The Department requests a notification when the drilling rig is removed from the pad. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection conducted an INCIDENT inspection at the SWEPI LP - Houck 433 well pad located in Shippen Twp, Tioga Co. on 3/11/2019 @1130 hours. Matt Skolny, SWEPI LP was present on the pony pad for the spill investigation. Morgan Davis, SWEPI LP OSR was present on the main pad. The weather was 37 degrees, sunny, winds WNW 15mph, the previously deposited snow is melting causing the site to the very muddy with standing water. April Heater, SWEPI LP reported a spill to the DEP's regional office on 3/8/2019 @1500 hours. Onsite personnel were breaking apart the "fastline", which was used to carry frack fluid from the AST on the pony pad to the main pad. Mr. Skolny stated they had run a number of courses of freshwater through the line to clean it out. When the line was dismantled the open end was placed in a tub, on secondary containment, on the NW corner of the pony pad. No fluid came out initially, but when the onsite personnel left to work on another area, fluid was discharged from the end of the pipe. The fluid overtopped containment, and entered the channel in the NW corner of the pad. SWEPI estimated `20 gallons of fluid was released into containent with `20 gallons overtopping and discharging into the perimeter E&S ditch. As of today's inspection, a tub of icy, black, frozen/slush mix that was initially recovered from the channel had a field measured conductivity of 3.0 mS/cm. This tub was placed on secondary containment for disposal. The channel off the edge of the pad was full of ice/snow with a small volume of liquid. No elevated conductivity was measured in the ditch or in puddles on the corner of the pony pad. A black greasy material and oily sheen was observed in the NW corner of the ditch. SWEPI was notified and instructed to have the material removed from the ditch. Matt Bailey was present onsite at this point, and stated he would have the remaining issues addressed. Due to the reported release of fluids onto the ground surface, violations of the following regulations are cited as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED at this time: 25 Pa Code 78a56(a) Temporary Storage SWMA 301 Solid Waste Management Act CSL 402(b) Potential Pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth An inspection of the main pad was also conducted. The coil rig was observed drilling out plugs on the 6H well on the main pad. Mr. Davis, SWEPI OSR accompanied me around the well pad during the inspection. A few areas of elevated conductivity were discovered inside containment. Mr. Davis stated he would have the fluid removed when the vac truck returned to the site. Mr. Davis was also notified of containment berms that appeared broken/smashed and were in need of repair. Although the site was very muddy, with large amounts of standing water, none of the puddles on the pad surface were found to have elevated conductivity. The E&S trap and rock-lined channels appeared frozen. No sedimentation or erosion was observed. I departed the site at 1345 hours.

Comments: On 04/07/2025 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Greylock Production LLCs Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1045 hours, weather was 34F and cloudy. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).Standing water observed on the pad surface field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at a range of ~310-332us/cm.There are 2 recently completed wells located onsite; the well permits are posted at the site entrance, however, I did not observe any tags on the wells (photo #2). 2 gas processing units (GPUs) are also located onsite (photo #3). The GPUs are held in a secondary containment structure which contained less than 10% standing water. There are 4 produced fluid tanks located onsite and stationed in secondary containment (photo #4); the containment structure contained less than 10% standing water. A dehydration unit is also noted onsite and is held in secondary containment (photo #5).Numerous temporary storage tanks are noted onsite for ongoing flow back activities, these tanks are held in secondary containment structures which retain sufficient storage capacity (photos #6 and 7). 6 upright brine storage tanks are also noted onsite but are not held in secondary containment (photo #8). 2 residual waste containers were also observed not held in secondary containment (photo #9).Perennial vegetative cover continues to grow in the areas surrounding the site (photo #10). No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. A weekly erosion and sediment (E and S) inspection log is available for review and is up to date (photo #11). 1 infiltration basin serves as the site's post construction stormwater management (PCSM) control (photos #12). No standing water was observed in the PCSM control and it appears to be functioning as intended.The DEP recommends the following:-Installing well tags on the wellheads. -Placing the upright brine storage tanks in secondary containment if they still contain a regulated substance to prevent violations from being cited against 25 PA 78a57(c).-Placing the residual waste containers in secondary containment.Violations noted in inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285 remain outstanding against API #105-21962 pending receipt of confirmation sampling and approval of Act 2 remediation standards.No additional violations noted. I departed the site at 1045 hours.

Comments: Arrived onsite in response to reported release of diesel fuel. The release occurred on the eastern side of the pad near the pipeline that is run to the site. The release was reported as at least 5 gallons of fuel. The location of the release was not near containment used for the recent drilling onsite. The source and total volume of the release were unknown at the time of inspection.Mr. Dirt was onsite excavating the impacted soil. The initial area marked for excavation was approximately 8' by 10'. The excavation increased to an irregular shape that was about 15' by 20' across and 8' deep. This increase in size was due in part to the stability of the excavated area causing the edges of the pit to break away. The impacted area was also excavated in a manner to ensure the complete removal of impacted soil.The removed material amounted to about 5 loads of soil that were 15 cubic yards per load. The soil was stored on secondary containment for the time being. Creston was also onsite collecting soil samples to verify that the remediation was sufficient.Based on the unknown volume of fuel released it is strongly recommended that Chesapeake remediate the location under Act 2 requirements. The result of this inspection Violations Noted for 78a56(a), SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b).

Comments: On 5/30/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Stoorza well site. It was 74 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. The site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by three retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed.There were two wells staged for production. Both wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The GPUs and production tank had secondary containment. A gas compressor is on site but was not running during the inspection.An inspection conducted by the department on 3/30/2023 described three waste piles of excavated material transported from the Chesapeake Grippo well site that had been temporarily stored at this location. These three piles have been removed from the Stoorza well site location along with the secondary containment structures. I viewed the areas of the pad surface and did not witness visible evidence of contamination. Due to the dry conditions in these locations, I could not screen the areas for conductance during this inspection.No violations were noted during this inspection.Violations are still outstanding for inspection IDs 3524618 and 3537962 for elevated conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface in proximity to stockpiles of contaminated excavated waste. Laboratory analysis determined the fluid contained high levels of barium, strontium and chlorides.I left the site at 1130 hours.

Comments: This site located west off Greeley Road north of junction with Francis Road in a forested area. Tank battery, two brine tanks and one oil tank in secondary containment, located along the access road. Marshall Wurst found this tank battery with a lined secondary containment containing a release of 2-3 bbls of crude oil on 8/23/2019. WQS Taylor inspected this site on 8/28/2019 and issued an NOV to Coastal Petro Corp. for the release of crude oil into the lined secondary containment. There was 1 1/2'-2' of crude oil/water in the secondary containment at the time of initial inspection. A follow-up inspection on 12/26/2020 found that the liquid crude oil/water mix that was in the secondary containment had been removed however there was snow and ice partially covering the bottom of the containment. Between this inspection and the last inspection water has collected in the secondary containment from recent precipitation events. Crude oil contamination is evident on the surface of the water and and on the outside of the tanks. An empty 200 gallon tote is set in the secondary containment between the oil tank and first brine tank. This well to be transferred from Coastal Petro Corp. to Titusville Oil & Gas Associates Inc., application for the transfer of wells was sent in on 11/18/2019. Titusville Oil & Gas Associates, Inc. is to complete the clean-up at this site.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/09/2024 to LEATHERWOOD LLC in Center Township, Greene county. 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect  brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: LEATHERWOOD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/09/2024
Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8200886
Permit API: 059-25626
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Center Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/09/2024
Comments: On 9/9/2024, I conducted an inspection at the Kentor Inc Well Pad following a produced fluid spill reported to the DEP Emergency Hotline by EQT on 9/6/2024 (CTS #383608). The spill was initially identified as staining on the ground that was discovered upon the removal of secondary containment for the Kentor 8H Well plugging operation. The spill was later updated to be greater than 5 gallons, but it was unclear the exact amount of produced fluid that was spilled onto the well pad.On site at the time of inspection was SPSI for spill remediation. SPSI indicated that they had remediated areas right of the plugged well, and a 30x60 foot area right of the plugged well was delineated by sandbags. SPSI stated that rain received on site on 9/6/2024 likely resulted in the produced fluid spill migrating out further across site. It was not clear at the time of inspection the cause of the spill nor how much produced fluid had spilled. A full spill delineation was not evident at the time of inspection. 2 rolloff boxes of impacted material were staged on site at the time of inspection, and SPSI was awaiting a third box to continue remediation.I spoke to Logan Dominick of EQT via phone call during my inspection who stated that the spill would likely be classified as an Act 2 Spill, and that the Kentor 8H Well was transferred to Leatherwood LLC to be plugged for mine-through.While on site I observed the following:-The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance and the access road appeared to be in generally good condition (Photos 1-3).-Aggregate staining as a result of produced fluid was evident immediately surrounding the left and right of the plugged well when entering the site. Aggregate was being excavated immediately around the plugged well at the time of inspection. I observed a range of conductivity readings in the stained aggregate surrounding the plugged well, varying from 2.18 mS/cm to 10.01 mS/cm. Standing fluid left of the plugged well appeared to have greater conductivity readings (Photos 4-12).-SPSI informed me while on site that they had discovered a soft spot in the aggregate on the well pad during initial remediation approximately 75-100 feet from the plugged well. Upon excavating this soft spot, produced fluid began filling up the hole. I observed conductivity readings of 10.01 mS/cm of the produced fluid standing within the hole, and the soil/aggregate read at 1859 us/cm (Photos 13-15).-Staining on the ground approximately 20 feet from the excavated hole with produced fluid within it resulted in normal conductivity measurements (Photo 16).-I observed conductivity readings of 5.65 mS/cm of standing fluid within the 30x60 ft spill delineation. Standing water located behind a black tarp at the edge of the delineated area demonstrated normal conductivity (Photos 17-21).-At the time of inspection, SPSI was excavating surficial aggregate/soil that was demonstrating overall conductivity readings of 4 mS/cm (Photos 22-23).-Standing fluid within a sump/trench dug near the left-side of the Kentor Well Site demonstrated normal conductivity (Photos 24-25).Violations of 91.34(A), 78a.57(a), 78a.54, and SWMA 301 are being issued for the spill. Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection of Repsol's OMR 02-188 well site located in Hamilton Township, Tioga County on 11/30/2022 at 0920 hours. The weather was 38 degrees with an overcast, light rain and moderate winds. The inspection was conducted in response to a release of produced water reported by the operator. Complaint tracking system (CTS) ID #368537 is tied to this release within CTSOn 11/29/2022 Repsol reported a 42 gallon release of produced water to the ground surface at the OMR 02-188 well site after a produced water flow-line was cut during the teardown process. Some produced water was initially pumped out of the line but not all was recovered prior to the cut of the flow-line. The produced water was then released to the ground in numerous areas along the flow-line. The impacted areas were then covered with tarps to help keep the areas free from the projected rain prior to excavation/remediation.During today's inspection, the impacted areas remained covered with tarps and a secondary containment liner to help prevent rain from spreading the release. Water present in the rock-lined channel located below the release area was field measured for electrical conductivity between 200us/cm to 380us/cm. Pad material and soils around the impacted areas covered by tarps were field measured for electrical conductivity between 0.1mS/cm and 0.3mS/cm. No evidence suggests that the release was able to reach the post-construction stormwater management (PCSM) controls.The operator was awaiting an 811 call approval and for the environmental consultant to arrive in order to begin remediation. Current estimations put an excavation start time at 1300 hours on 11/30/2022. Discussion with an operator representative onsite places the release estimate at ~42 gallons, or one barrel, but it is not exactly known. Current rainfall would have a chance to commingle with the release prior to total recovery. Photos of the initial release discovery were provided to me via email. The operator explained that Act 2 sampling was planned to be conducted.Based on the reported release of 42 gallons of produced water to the ground, violations of the following are cited against API #117-22132 at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.57(a)35 P.S. 6018.30135 P.S. 691.402(b)I departed the site at 1020 hours.

Comments: On January 29, 2026, the Department conducted an Incident Inspection at Range Resources Shearer Robert tank pad located in Robinson Township, Washington County following a spill that was reported to the DEP on 1/27/2026. Accompanying during today's inspection was Range Resources representative Nate Smiell.Documented in IR 4131333, according to the spill report and the phone conversation with Mr. Zofchak, at approximately 2:55 AM on January 27, 2026 a water truck was staged on the tank pad when a closed valve on the back of the truck began leaking into a bleeder valve hose, subsequently releasing Produced Water onto the gravel pad in an approximately 20 ft by 100 ft area. Water truck drivers contained the release to the graveledwell pad and began vacuuming up the pooled fluid, SPSI arrived on site on 1/27/2026 and began scraping the gravel tank pad. The release was estimated to be approximately 193 gallons, and no waters of the Commonwealth were reportedly impacted.At the time of this inspection, an Act 9 sign was observed at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it and in the on-site mailbox was an Emergency Response Plan, and a Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency Plan, both of which had all required components.At the time of this inspection, Mr. Smiell showed the Department the approximate location of the incident area and stated that SPSI finished scraping the tank pad and filled 2 roll off dumpsters with contaminated gravel on 1/27/2026. The area which appeared to be approximately 100 ft by 20 ft was observed to be recently scraped. Some spray paint was observed on the gravel to mark the areas where Mr. Smiell reported that samples were collected on 1/28/2026 in accordance with Act 2 requirements. Soil conductivity readings could not be collected due to the ground being frozen, however, the Department did not observe any visible evidence of Produced Water remaining on the graveled tank pad. Range is requested to submit a written response within 15 days of the receipt of this report. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, and plan for remediation of the violations. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled.Range will need to follow the Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2).Range will also need to assess the impacts to waters of the Commonwealth from the release.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the 193 gallon release of Produced Water onto the graveled tank pad.

Comments: On January 29, 2026, the Department conducted an Incident Inspection at Range Resources Shearer Robert tank pad located in Robinson Township, Washington County following a spill that was reported to the DEP on 1/27/2026. Accompanying during today's inspection was Range Resources representative Nate Smiell.Documented in IR 4131333, according to the spill report and the phone conversation with Mr. Zofchak, at approximately 2:55 AM on January 27, 2026 a water truck was staged on the tank pad when a closed valve on the back of the truck began leaking into a bleeder valve hose, subsequently releasing Produced Water onto the gravel pad in an approximately 20 ft by 100 ft area. Water truck drivers contained the release to the graveledwell pad and began vacuuming up the pooled fluid, SPSI arrived on site on 1/27/2026 and began scraping the gravel tank pad. The release was estimated to be approximately 193 gallons, and no waters of the Commonwealth were reportedly impacted.At the time of this inspection, an Act 9 sign was observed at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it and in the on-site mailbox was an Emergency Response Plan, and a Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency Plan, both of which had all required components.At the time of this inspection, Mr. Smiell showed the Department the approximate location of the incident area and stated that SPSI finished scraping the tank pad and filled 2 roll off dumpsters with contaminated gravel on 1/27/2026. The area which appeared to be approximately 100 ft by 20 ft was observed to be recently scraped. Some spray paint was observed on the gravel to mark the areas where Mr. Smiell reported that samples were collected on 1/28/2026 in accordance with Act 2 requirements. Soil conductivity readings could not be collected due to the ground being frozen, however, the Department did not observe any visible evidence of Produced Water remaining on the graveled tank pad. Comments: On October 18 2024 the Department conducted an inspection in regards to a spill reported under CTS 384608. Present during the inspection were operator representatives Paul Stiner and Bryan Goletz.The findings are as follows:Upon talking to the operator while onsite, it was stated that a check valve had broke causing a pressure build up to occur in the underground poly flow line, resulting in the line to fail. The failure in the poly line caused roughly 55 barrels of brine to be released into the ground. The release was observed by the operator at roughly 12 pm on 10/18/24, and reported to the Department at 1:17pm on 10/18/2024 . While onsite, the Department observed Penn Plus onsite beginning remediation efforts. According to Mr.Stiner, triaxle trucks are to arrive to the site on 10/21/2024, and all impacted soil would be excavated and disposed of. The operator stated because of the size of the release, they will be under going Act 2 remediation, with Moody preparing all of the related Act 2 documents/reports.Upon inspection of the location of the spill, the Department observed what appeared to be the location of the failure in the poly line (photos 1 and 2). A conductivity reading was taken in this location with a reading of "OR" (Out of range of maximum readings).The Department observed puddles of fluid on the surface of the well site (photos 5-7). The Department observed a tanker truck onsite using suction hoses to remove the excess fluid/puddles from the ground. Conductivity readings were taken with in the puddles as well as downslope from the location of the poly line failure with multiple readings of "OR". Elevated readings (9.22mS) were detected roughly 175 feet down slope (east) of the failure. Mr.Stiner stated he had obtained elevated readings approximately 180 feet from the poly line failure and the depth of contamination appeared to be roughly 2 feet (photo 14). No impacts to waters of the commonwealth were observed.The Department recommends the operator follows the Department's Spill Policy and October 3 2014 Program Clarification Memo for remediation of the spill. The Department requests the waste manifest for the impacted material upon receipt.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 business days of the spill or release.This response should include an incident report, a timeline, the regulation substance involved, where the spill or release occur, the environmental media affected, any impacts to water supplies, buildings, or utilities, and interim actions planned, initiated, or completed.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. Any new impacts discovered or identified during interim remedial actions or site characterization should also be reported to the Department within 15 calendar days of discovery.Within 180 days of the spill or release the operator must perform a site characterization to determine the extent and magnitude of the contamination and submit the site characterization report to the undersigned.Based on todays inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release.

The Department observed a tanker truck onsite using suction hoses to remove the excess fluid/puddles from the ground. Conductivity readings were taken with in the puddles as well as downslope from the location of the poly line failure with multiple readings of "OR". Elevated readings (9.22mS) were detected roughly 175 feet down slope (east) of the failure. Mr.Stiner stated he had obtained elevated readings approximately 180 feet from the poly line failure and the depth of contamination appeared to be roughly 2 feet (photo 14). No impacts to waters of the commonwealth were observed.The Department recommends the operator follows the Department's Spill Policy and October 3 2014 Program Clarification Memo for remediation of the spill. The Department requests the waste manifest for the impacted material upon receipt.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 business days of the spill or release.This response should include an incident report, a timeline, the regulation substance involved, where the spill or release occur, the environmental media affected, any impacts to water supplies, buildings, or utilities, and interim actions planned, initiated, or completed.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. Any new impacts discovered or identified during interim remedial actions or site characterization should also be reported to the Department within 15 calendar days of discovery.Within 180 days of the spill or release the operator must perform a site characterization to determine the extent and magnitude of the contamination and submit the site characterization report to the undersigned.Based on todays inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release.

Comments: Inspection conducted in response to a notification from the operator of a release of produced water which occurred during fracing operations. In a follow-up email sent on 6/1/20 by Mike Deming of SWN, the estimated release volume was decreased to less than 20 gallons. The size of the excavation area was 20 ft by 25 ft and an average depth of 2 inches. The estimated volume of material excavated was reported as less than 1 cubic yard. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.
